proof_boundary: This gate proves nilpotent ideal-cubic transport and collar variation estimates. It proves no numerical retained-observation bound, grouped ideal-cubic c-prime or roster estimate, endpoint cancellation, quadratic residual bound, signed flow estimate, Phi_B upper bound, contact exclusion, retained aggregate or Xi theorem, Lambda<=0, PF-infinity, RH, or prize-level conclusion.

rows.claim: The surviving ideal cubic is generated by one four-vector polynomial.
rows.proof_boundary: The correction-driven difference remains governed by Section 11.176.

rows.claim: The four-vector field has one constant nilpotent generator.
rows.proof_boundary: This is an algebraic transport identity, not a phase estimate.

rows.certificate: The row direction (0,0,1,-1) annihilates F_0(x) identically, so only alpha_A+alpha_Q and beta_A+beta_Q survive.
rows.claim: The ideal channel identifies the A and Q field directions.
rows.proof_boundary: The physical corrections need not preserve this exact null direction.

rows.certificate: Y(x)=(F_0(x),xF_0(x))^T. Dhat=[[D_0,0],[I_4,D_0]], with Dhat^4=0 but Dhat^3!=0. Y'=Dhat Y and Y(x)=exp(xDhat)Y(0), where the exponential terminates after its cubic term.
rows.claim: The base and lifted fields form one order-four nilpotent jet.
rows.proof_boundary: Both retained rows remain inside one augmented row.

rows.certificate: bar(P)=(alpha^T,i beta^T)Y; its four coefficients are the Section 11.175 bar(gamma)_0,...,bar(gamma)_3.
rows.claim: The augmented row reproduces all four ideal coefficients.
rows.proof_boundary: No numerical retained-row bound is inserted.

rows.claim: The physical Morse operator is a small perturbation of one constant nilpotent core.
rows.proof_boundary: Small operator perturbation does not make the row contraction small.

rows.claim: The removable saddle operator is one explicit matrix polynomial.
rows.proof_boundary: The full c-prime integral still contains its Fresnel and endpoint geometry.

rows.certificate: At t=epsilon_g=0, M_0=Dhat^2-I_8/12 and det(M_0)=12^(-8), so nilpotence supplies transport but no universal saddle zero.
rows.claim: The ideal saddle core is invertible rather than identically canceling.
rows.proof_boundary: Nilpotent transport supplies no universal saddle zero or sign.

rows.claim: The physical saddle matrix stays uniformly close to its constant core.
rows.proof_boundary: This is a matrix coefficient bound, not a roster sum.

rows.claim: Adjacent logarithmic modes have one exact step law.
rows.proof_boundary: The fixed roster and endpoint crossings remain unchanged.

rows.claim: Every ideal joined field shifts by a terminating cubic exponential.
rows.proof_boundary: No numerical mode enumeration is required.

rows.claim: The variation of the logarithmic step is exactly the normalized phase curvature.
rows.proof_boundary: This bridge is local to the certified terminal collar.

rows.certificate: Using ||Dhat||_1=2, ||Dhat^2||_1=5/2, and ||Dhat^3||_1=3/2, the exact transport gives ||Y_(r+1)-Y_r||_1<(9/(4alpha))||Y_r||_1.
rows.claim: The ideal joined field has O(alpha^-1) first variation on the collar.

rows.claim: The ideal joined field has O(alpha^-2) second variation on the collar.
rows.proof_boundary: This does not by itself improve the existing phase partial-sum theorem.

rows.proof_boundary: Its joined row contraction and Fresnel integral are not bounded here.
